author: Arabella B. Buckley
title: Eyes and No Eyes
edition: Undated Cassell and Company, Ltd printing (imprint London, Toronto, Melbourne and Sydney; “Printed in Great Britain”) of the one-volume Eyes and No Eyes, “With Forty-Eight Full Page Coloured Plates”, author named as Arabella B. Buckley (Mrs. Fisher); York University Libraries copy, Internet Archive eyesnoeyes00buck, catalogued 1903. That one-volume edition was first published by Cassell in March 1902: The English Catalogue of Books, vol. VII (1901–1905), lists “Buckley (Arabella B.)—Eyes and No Eyes. 48 Clrd. Plates, other Illus. Cr. 8vo. 3s. 6d. Cassell, Mar. 02”, and vol. X (1916–1920) records a Cassell reissue in February 1920. The scanned printing is one of these issues or a reprint of them; its own date is unknown, so publicationYear gives the 1902 first publication of the text. The nightly readings use whole lessons of Book I, Wild Life in Woods and Fields (Introduction and Lessons II–VI, VIII and XII). Gateway to the Classics HTML served only as a typing aid; every nightly paragraph was collated with the scan by full-text OCR comparison and page-image checks, and 22 typing-aid errors were corrected. Printed defects are reproduced, including sentence-final stops missing from the print on pp. 11, 17 and 18. Print line wraps joined, line-end split-word hyphens removed, initial small capitals in normal capitalization, typographic quotation marks represented by straight quotes; plates and captions excluded. The library text is the whole volume, not only the nightly lessons: Buckley's preface (signed “Arabella B. Buckley (Mrs. Fisher)”), Books I–VI with the notes to teachers she printed under the contents of Books III–VI, and the table of insect orders at the end of Book VI, in 1,199 blocks (7 level-1 headings for the volume title and the six Books, 83 level-2 headings, 1,108 paragraphs and 1 stanza). Outside the nightly passages the text was established from the scan in the same way: OCR of the scan was collated word by word with Gateway to the Classics. Each of the 1,940 disagreements was settled by a page-image check (935) or by one of two mechanical rules checked on a sample of crops (1,005). The print wins throughout: 26 sentence-final stops missing from the print are reproduced, and so are a few other printed readings that differ from Gateway (for example “were only recently repaired” in Book V). The author's cross-references such as “(See p. 8.)” are kept, and the one footnote, on p. 43, is given as “[Footnote *: …]” after its paragraph, with its anchor written “[*]”. The publisher's series line, plates, captions, running heads, page numbers and leader dots are omitted. Em dashes are closed up, and line-end hyphens follow how the same word is printed mid-line elsewhere in the book.

rights.basis: The text was first published in the United Kingdom by Cassell in March 1902 (one-volume edition with 48 coloured plates; English Catalogue of Books vol. VII) and reissued in February 1920 (vol. X); the scanned printing carries no later copyright claim. Publication before 1931 places the text in the US public domain as of 2026. The printing date of the scanned copy itself is unknown. The whole volume’s text is supplied, without plates, captions, or modern editorial matter.

acquisition.method: Downloads, in order (downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the 91 responses concatenated in this order): Internet Archive eyesnoeyes00buck_abbyy.gz, eyesnoeyes00buck_djvu.xml and eyesnoeyes00buck.pdf (https://archive.org/download/eyesnoeyes00buck/); then 88 Gateway to the Classics pages, http://www.gatewaytotheclassics.com/browse/display.php?author=buckley&book={book}&story={story}. The Gateway pages are wildlife/_front (preface) and then, for each book, its _contents page followed by its lesson pages: wildlife: _contents, intro, spiders, nest, flowers, squirrels, skylark, nuts, mouse, ant, humble, cat, greedy, mole; pond: _contents, life, dragonfly, below, nest, kingfisher, rat, coot, bugs, river, otter, flowers, plants; plant: _contents, purse, work, turnip, grows, making, insects, eat, cabbage, defend, wild, rose, pea, climbing, store, underground, travel; birds: _contents, know, song, nests, eggs, baby, feeding, sleep, summer, migrating, winter, small, prey, rooks, web, enemies; trees: _contents, value, starts, grows, catkin, oak, guests, beech, cones, hedge, bloom, ash, park, leaves; insect: _contents, what, parts, moths, butter, beetles, useful, wasps, bees, hive, flies, crickets, ants; Pipeline: ABBYY words were put into reading order by page position. Running heads, page numbers, signature marks, figure and plate captions, and the table of insect orders were classed by position and type size. Gateway lesson HTML was parsed into paragraphs with _italics_. The two token streams were aligned per unit (preface, Books I–VI) with difflib SequenceMatcher on lowercased alphanumeric keys: 68,279 tokens agree and 1,940 disagree (1,458 word, 355 punctuation or case, 75 italics, 52 paragraph breaks). Resolution: 935 by viewing a crop of the page image (874 at 200 dpi, 61 more at 400 dpi). In those checks the print matched the OCR 177 times and Gateway 484 times, 20 needed an explicit reading, 127 OCR or Gateway insertions were dropped, 52 were paragraph decisions and 75 italic decisions. The other 1,005 were settled mechanically. If the OCR word is outside the Gateway vocabulary, at least 50% similar to Gateway's reading, and neither a compound of known words nor an ABBYY dictionary word, Gateway's reading is taken (840). OCR-only text classed as non-text is dropped (165). Both rules were verified before use on a random sample of 75 crops: 48 of 50 garbled readings confirmed at 200 dpi and the other 2 at 400 dpi as damaged type, and 25 of 25 drops were captions, running heads, page numbers or signature marks. Line-end hyphens in the OCR were kept or removed by mid-line evidence in the volume: 161 joined, 54 kept; ties follow Gateway, 28 kept and 20 joined; image-checked exceptions are recorded with the decisions. All 83 level-2 headings, the six Book heads, the preface heading and signature, the Book III–VI notes and the p. 417 table were transcribed from page images. Every Kindergarten night from this book was located block for block.
